inquiry_commissioners.name: Justice Murray Sinclair
inquiry_commissioners.notable: First Indigenous judge in Manitoba (1988). Led the TRC 2009-2015, producing the 6-volume Final Report (2015) and 94 Calls to Action. Later Senator (2016-2021). His TRC findings are the authoritative Canadian government-commissioned record of the residential school system.

inquiry_commissioners.name: Marion Buller
inquiry_commissioners.role: Chief Commissioner, National Inquiry into MMIWG
inquiry_commissioners.notable: First Indigenous woman appointed judge in BC (1994). Chief Commissioner of the National Inquiry into Missing and Murdered Indigenous Women and Girls 2016-2019. Her Final Report (2019) issued 231 Calls for Justice and found the deaths constituted a 'genocide' under Canadian and international law.

crown_indigenous_ministers.name: Carolyn Bennett
crown_indigenous_ministers.notable: Six-year tenure spanning the TRC implementation period and the MMIWG Inquiry. Tabled multiple Indigenous-rights bills. Responsible for the Crown-Indigenous Relations file during Kamloops 215 unmarked graves disclosure (May 2021).

crown_indigenous_ministers.name: Marc Miller
crown_indigenous_ministers.notable: Crown-Indigenous 2021-2023. Previously Indigenous Services 2019-2021. Oversaw post-Kamloops response and continued residential-schools burial investigations. Later moved to Immigration 2023.

crown_indigenous_ministers.name: Gary Anandasangaree
crown_indigenous_ministers.notable: Crown-Indigenous 2023-2025. Responsible for implementation of UN Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples (UNDRIP) Act 2021.

indigenous_services_ministers.name: Jane Philpott
indigenous_services_ministers.notable: Inaugural Minister of Indigenous Services (portfolio split from Indian Affairs in 2017). Previously Health Minister 2015-2017. Resigned from cabinet 2019 over SNC-Lavalin affair.

indigenous_services_ministers.name: Patty Hajdu
indigenous_services_ministers.notable: Moved to Indigenous Services from Health 2021. Held the portfolio during the 2021-2023 expansion of First Nations water infrastructure commitments and ongoing boil-water advisory failures.

indigenous_services_ministers.name: Patty Hajdu / successor arc
indigenous_services_ministers.notable: Portfolio continuity placeholder for successor minister tracking under the Trudeau-to-Carney transition. Tracking: boil-water advisories still active in 2025 despite 2015 commitment to eliminate.

justice_ministers_indigenous_file.name: Jody Wilson-Raybould
justice_ministers_indigenous_file.role: Minister of Justice, Attorney General of Canada
justice_ministers_indigenous_file.notable: First Indigenous Justice Minister / AG in Canadian history. Member of We Wai Kai Nation. Resigned from cabinet February 2019 over SNC-Lavalin pressure. Her tenure spanned the Missing and Murdered Indigenous Women inquiry establishment (2016).

justice_ministers_indigenous_file.name: David Lametti
justice_ministers_indigenous_file.role: Minister of Justice, Attorney General of Canada
justice_ministers_indigenous_file.notable: Justice 2019-2023. Tabled UNDRIP Act implementation legislation. Cross-axis: also in MAID dossier (tabled C-7). Responsibility for MMIWG Calls for Justice implementation in criminal-justice domain.

afn_national_chiefs.name: Perry Bellegarde
afn_national_chiefs.role: Assembly of First Nations National Chief
afn_national_chiefs.notable: Two-term AFN National Chief spanning the TRC Final Report release (2015), the MMIWG Inquiry establishment (2016), the UNDRIP Act (2021), and the Kamloops 215 disclosure (May 2021). Advocated for the 94 Calls to Action.

afn_national_chiefs.name: RoseAnne Archibald
afn_national_chiefs.role: Assembly of First Nations National Chief (first woman)
afn_national_chiefs.notable: First woman elected AFN National Chief. Suspended by AFN Executive Committee amid governance dispute; removed 2023. Her tenure covered the continued unmarked graves disclosures and pandemic-era Indigenous health crises.

afn_national_chiefs.name: Cindy Woodhouse Nepinak
afn_national_chiefs.role: Assembly of First Nations National Chief
afn_national_chiefs.notable: Current AFN National Chief. Holds the position during the Carney government's opening moves on Indigenous file implementation.

prime_ministers_of_record.name: Stephen Harper
prime_ministers_of_record.notable: Issued the 2008 formal Statement of Apology to former students of Indian Residential Schools on behalf of the Government of Canada. Established the Truth and Reconciliation Commission (2008). Nine-year PM; TRC Final Report published under his successor.

prime_ministers_of_record.name: Justin Trudeau
prime_ministers_of_record.notable: Nine-year PM. Committed to implementing all 94 TRC Calls to Action in 2015. As of 2025, Yellowhead Institute tracking finds only ~13 of 94 fully implemented. Delivered federal statement of apology on 2021 Kamloops disclosure. Oversaw MMIWG National Inquiry and 231 Calls for Justice.

prime_ministers_of_record.name: Mark Carney
prime_ministers_of_record.notable: Current PM. Holds responsibility for continued TRC Calls to Action implementation, UNDRIP Act enforcement, and ongoing boil-water advisory commitments inherited from Trudeau era. Cross-axis: also in Carney-Brookfield dossier as central figure.

timeline.event: PM Harper's formal Statement of Apology to former students of Indian Residential Schools, delivered in the House of Commons.
Truth and Reconciliation Commission established under the Indian Residential Schools Settlement Agreement.
Justice Murray Sinclair appointed TRC Chair.
TRC Final Report Volume 1 released. 94 Calls to Action published.
Trudeau government takes office, committing to implement all 94 Calls to Action.
National Inquiry into Missing and Murdered Indigenous Women and Girls established.
Indigenous Services portfolio split from Indian Affairs. Jane Philpott sworn in as inaugural Minister.
MMIWG Final Report: 'Reclaiming Power and Place.' 231 Calls for Justice. Finds deaths constitute 'genocide.'
Tk'emlúps te Secwépemc Nation announces detection of approximately 215 unmarked graves at former Kamloops Indian Residential School.
UNDRIP Act (Bill C-15) receives Royal Assent. Canada implements the UN Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples.
Cowessess First Nation announces 751 unmarked graves at former Marieval Indian Residential School.
Yellowhead Institute annual report: of 94 Calls to Action, only 11 fully implemented.
Yellowhead Institute annual report: 13 of 94 Calls to Action fully implemented.
Yellowhead Institute annual report: 13 of 94 Calls to Action fully implemented — progress stalled.
Carney government takes office. Indigenous-file implementation commitments carried forward.

statutory_framework: Constitution Act, 1982 — s. 35 Aboriginal and Treaty Rights
UN Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act — S.C. 2021, c. 14 (UNDRIP Act)
Indian Residential Schools Settlement Agreement (2007, court-approved)
commissions_and_inquiries: Royal Commission on Aboriginal Peoples (1991-1996) — RCAP Final Report, 440 recommendations
Truth and Reconciliation Commission (2008-2015) — 94 Calls to Action
National Inquiry into MMIWG (2016-2019) — 231 Calls for Justice
implementation_tracking: Yellowhead Institute — TRC Calls to Action Tracker (annual)
Government of Canada — Indigenous Services annual reports
accountability_chain.result_2025: Of 94 TRC Calls to Action (2015): ~13 fully implemented. Of 231 MMIWG Calls for Justice (2019): implementation tracker fragmented. Boil-water advisories committed for elimination by 2021 remain active on 31+ First Nations communities. 'Genocide' finding of MMIWG accepted by Trudeau government but without criminal-law follow-through.
